prompt: Read the current Introduction and discuss its argument. Do not modify any file.
must: bind the review to the current manuscript snapshot
report findings without writing project files
separate framing problems from prose preferences
must_not: edit the manuscript
create persistent project state without authorization
rewrite the section as the default response

prompt: Edit the named paragraph in the manuscript file in place and reduce it by exactly five words. Do not alter the surrounding text or substantive meaning.
must: freeze the authorized span and neighboring text
use one explicit word-count rule before and after
inspect the local diff and report an exact five-word reduction
explain the substantive compression with one bold governing-principle tag outside the manuscript
must_not: rewrite the whole paragraph
remove a qualifier, denominator, citation, or logical bridge
change adjacent text

prompt: Revise the Introduction to match the latest evidence, but the submitted title and abstract are locked.
must: record the title and abstract as immutable
propagate only compatible changes through the authorized Introduction
flag any conflict that cannot be resolved without changing locked text
must_not: edit the title
edit the abstract
silently weaken or strengthen the evidence

prompt: Using the supplied paper contract and claim-evidence map, draft a new Results section. No manuscript text exists for this section yet.
must: define the section contract and organize results by inferential question
trace every quantitative or qualitative conclusion to the supplied evidence
preserve aggregation, uncertainty, exceptions, and claim boundaries
must_not: invent a result, citation, mechanism, or missing protocol detail
narrate a table or figure cell by cell
strengthen the claim to make the section sound more decisive

prompt: We have an early research idea and several possible stories, but no settled novelty claim. Help determine the strongest defensible framing before drafting.
must: compare candidate problem formulations and contribution types
test them against closest work and available evidence
record why rejected alternatives fail
must_not: draft a confident novelty claim before the comparison
invent a research gap
treat an appealing story as established evidence

prompt: Our novelty claim and Related Work comparison currently rely on the abstracts of several neighboring papers. Audit what we can state before revising the manuscript.
must: split the novelty claim into source-checkable propositions
require full-text verification for differences in assumptions, inputs, outputs, mechanisms, or evidence
state the current search status without treating missing retrievals as proof of absence
must_not: declare priority from abstracts alone
invent citation details or technical distinctions
rewrite the manuscript before the closest-work boundary is established

prompt: Review only. The theorem covers finite objects under two explicit assumptions, while the title and abstract call the result universal.
must: reconstruct the theorem's quantifiers, domain, and assumptions
identify the mismatch between proved scope and headline claim
propose the strongest bounded interpretation without editing files
must_not: treat a broad motivation as a proved theorem
remove assumptions from the claim
edit the title or abstract during a read-only review

prompt: The Method says a quantity is available at inference, but the executed code appears to derive it from the target. Audit the discrepancy before changing prose.
must: build an information-availability table by pipeline stage
trace the quantity from manuscript notation to executed code
state the resulting claim and leakage risk
must_not: hide the conflict through vague wording
assume the manuscript or code is correct without inspection
edit the paper before the behavior is established

prompt: The proposed approach changes information access, measurement procedure, and analysis together and improves the endpoint over the comparator. Audit the comparison and propose the strongest defensible result sentence.
must: identify every changed and controlled variable
attribute the result to the matched whole-system comparison
state which component-level mechanisms remain unidentified
must_not: credit one component without an isolating comparison
describe correlation as mechanism
omit relevant information or resource-budget differences

prompt: A perturbation diagnostic changes the reported response for every group. Explain what this establishes.
must: describe the finding as functional dependence or sensitivity
define the perturbation and validity boundary
separate diagnostic sensitivity from the correctness of a real-world counterfactual
must_not: claim causal identification
claim a correct real-world counterfactual response
call sensitivity an accuracy metric

prompt: Review the evidence for a qualitative finding derived from selected interview excerpts and presented as a general population conclusion.
must: trace the theme to the sampling and analytic procedure
distinguish representative excerpts from the full evidential chain
bound transfer or population claims to the study design
must_not: treat a vivid quotation as population prevalence
impose a quantitative significance test by default
dismiss qualitative evidence because it is not numerical

prompt: The primary endpoint and exclusion rule were selected after viewing the final outcomes. Audit the strongest claim the study can now support.
must: distinguish exploratory from prespecified evidence
record the timing and consequence of endpoint and exclusion choices
state what independent confirmation would be needed for a confirmatory claim
must_not: describe the choices as prespecified
discard the exploratory finding as automatically worthless
present the selected endpoint as confirmatory without qualification

prompt: Design the paper's central multi-panel figure from existing results and representative examples.
must: assign a primary claim family to the figure and a distinct subordinate role to each panel
record data sources, transformations, scales, and selection rules
distinguish representative examples from population evidence
must_not: select a favorable case without disclosure
use unmatched scales for a magnitude comparison
let the caption claim more than the visual establishes

prompt: Check the current submission rules, anonymity, page limits, supplementary package, and required files for a named venue, year, and track.
must: verify the exact venue, year, track, and submission stage
use current official sources
separate mandatory requirements from recommendations
must_not: reuse remembered rules from another year
treat a template example as the authoritative policy
claim readiness without inspecting rendered artifacts

prompt: Apply an approved section revision, but the manuscript file changed after your initial read.
must: re-read the current file and compare it with the starting snapshot
preserve the other author's new intent
rebase only the authorized semantic change and inspect the diff
must_not: overwrite the newer file with an older draft
restore language that the author deleted
apply an unbounded global replacement

prompt: Translate this technical passage into concise academic English without changing its claims, notation, citations, or uncertainty.
must: preserve logical direction, modality, terminology, and citation scope
translate the scientific relation rather than source syntax
flag any ambiguity that requires a scientific decision
must_not: strengthen novelty or causality
cycle canonical technical terms
add examples or explanations absent from the source

prompt: Review only. A collaborator supplied several manuscript comments. Some make factual claims about the code and cited papers without showing evidence, one proposes a useful deletion for an incorrect reason, and one is purely a style preference. Decide what should be adopted.
must: separate factual premises, scientific risks, evidence requests, prose preferences, and policy judgments
verify material premises against their responsible sources
assign accept, partially accept, reject, or unresolved to each comment and judge its rationale separately from its action
must_not: implement a comment because the reviewer or collaborator sounds authoritative
discard a useful correction only because its stated rationale is wrong
present an uninspected source claim as verified

prompt: Diagnose only. Two adjacent sentences use 'therefore' although the second does not follow from the first, and the next pair uses 'however' without a genuine contrast. Explain the prose defect without rewriting the passage.
must: name the actual or missing relation between each adjacent sentence pair
state the logical prerequisites of the connectives
recommend repairing the reasoning, order, or missing proposition
must_not: replace one connective with another as the whole remedy
invent evidence to create a relation
rewrite the passage during detect-only work

prompt: Review only. A general method equation permits an optional input, the reported configuration disables it, the executed benchmark never varies it, and the abstract says the study demonstrates the corresponding capability.
must: separate what the design permits, configuration enables, procedure executes, evaluation tests, and result establishes
trace the optional input through configuration and executed behavior
bound the manuscript claim at the furthest verified status
must_not: treat a general equation as evidence that the option was active
treat implemented support as evaluated capability
claim a demonstrated effect without a relevant result

prompt: Plan a central figure that combines raw observations, a derived metric, scientific model outputs, a reconstruction, a conceptual schematic, and presentation-only generated artwork.
must: assign each panel an explicit evidence identity and inferential role
record the source and transformation for measured or computed panels
visually distinguish and disclose schematics and generated illustrations
must_not: present generated artwork as an observation or scientific model output
treat all panels as independent empirical confirmations
leave the reconstruction or derived metric unlabeled

prompt: Audit a Results paragraph that calls one benchmark OOD, robust, physical, zero-shot, real-time, and uncertainty-aware without defining any of those terms.
must: treat every broad evaluation label as a claim
request the exact changed or held-out axis, operation, reference, metric, and scope needed for each label
replace unsupported labels with narrower operational descriptions
must_not: accept labels as self-explanatory benchmark names
infer causality or counterfactual validity from perturbation alone
call a latency result real-time without a measurement boundary and criterion

prompt: Audit only. The checklist says code and data are currently available, the submission archive contains neither, and the manuscript promises release after acceptance.
must: distinguish current access, inclusion with submission, release upon acceptance, release after publication, and unavailability
verify the actual package or access route
require consistent status and tense across the checklist, manuscript, archive, and metadata
must_not: treat a future release promise as current availability
mark the package compliant without inspecting it
silently rewrite conflicting availability claims

prompt: Audit only. An early framing says the topic is increasingly important and immediately introduces a method, but never identifies who needs the result, what decision or scientific inquiry it supports, or what has changed to make the work timely.
must: recover the scenario, stakeholder or scientific audience, decision, inquiry, or use, and objective independently of the method
separate established value from prospective downstream impact
require evidence for any why-now claim or omit it when no enabling change is established
must_not: treat the method itself as proof that the problem matters
invent a commercial user or deployment decision for a basic-science paper
use increasing importance as a substitute for a verified enabling change

prompt: The initial search used only the proposed method name and found no direct match. Plan a literature audit before making a novelty or priority claim.
must: search field taxonomies, failures and assumptions, mechanism terms, neighboring disciplines, evaluation or deployment critiques, and falsifying evidence
compare retrieved work by problem and information contract rather than keywords alone
record unresolved search directions and retrieval limits
must_not: declare novelty from a method-name search
treat no retrieved source as proof of absence
search only for papers that support the proposed framing

prompt: Audit only. A technical section introduces a fully defined auxiliary function, three quantiles, and two equations that are never used again and are not needed to understand or reproduce the method.
must: judge whether each formal object has a necessary technical or reader role before asking for more definitions
recommend the simplest operational description that preserves any necessary behavior
remove dispensable notation even when it is mathematically correct
must_not: retain the equations merely because every symbol can be defined
add more notation to repair an unnecessary formalism
confuse mathematical completeness with manuscript value

prompt: Perform a final, exhaustive review of this manuscript. Previous passes relied on keyword searches and compilation diagnostics and missed local prose, equation, and caption problems.
must: traverse sections, paragraphs, sentences, equations, tables, figures, captions, and references in document order
record a completion status for every applicable unit
use searches and linting only as supplements to the sequential traversal
must_not: claim a full audit after inspecting only search hits or selected sections
treat a clean compile as a content review
omit the unit classes or scope that were not checked

prompt: Detect only. A Results passage repeatedly says that bands are not confidence intervals, panels do not prove gains, route values are not comparable, and a diagnostic is not an accuracy metric, although the corresponding constructs can be defined directly.
must: separate necessary construct boundaries from internal reviewer-facing caveats
prefer positive operational definitions where they prevent the same misreading
retain a negative boundary only when its omission would materially distort the claim
must_not: delete a scientifically necessary limitation as mere style
leave every audit non-conclusion in the manuscript
replace defensive prose with a stronger unsupported claim

prompt: Audit a setup section containing several precise totals and configuration counts that are traceable in code but appear without decomposition, source, role, or interpretive value.
must: distinguish numerical traceability from reader-facing usefulness
decompose totals whose factors explain the study design and identify the source or role of fixed counts
replace or remove exact values that add neither interpretation nor promised reproducibility
must_not: retain a magic number solely because it can be found in a configuration file
invent a rationale for a value
remove a denominator or count needed to reconstruct a headline result

prompt: Audit every result figure and table. Their captions describe panels but make no data-backed observation, and several annotations were copied from an older result snapshot.
must: trace plotted values and caption statistics to the responsible data, analysis, and plotting path
give each result-bearing visual one bounded source-verified observation
keep multi-visual synthesis in the Results text rather than overloading one caption
must_not: infer a quantitative caption claim from visual appearance
force an empirical conclusion into a schematic or method diagram
reuse an older caption as numerical ground truth

prompt: The submission PDF passed the final audit, but another process recompiled it afterward. The path is unchanged while the hash and file size differ.
must: invalidate every check that depended on the previous binary
re-run rendered, size, font, metadata, and visual checks on the exact upload file
record the final path, size, hash, last affecting operation, and unresolved warnings
must_not: transfer readiness from the old hash to the new file
treat an unchanged filename as an unchanged artifact
declare readiness before the regenerated binary is inspected

prompt: A submission PDF exceeds its verified size limit. Most pages are already compliant, while three high-resolution raster objects dominate the embedded size and the remaining figures are vector or near the minimum resolution.
must: diagnose embedded PDF object sizes rather than ranking source assets alone
preserve vector content and selectively reduce only raster assets that materially affect the limit
revalidate page count, size, minimum resolution, fonts, metadata, and visual legibility
must_not: rasterize or globally recompress the whole document without diagnosis
judge success from source-image size alone
accept an output that meets the size limit by violating resolution or font requirements

prompt: The manuscript PDF is anonymous, but plotting provenance and metric files considered for the submission archive contain private absolute paths and a user identifier.
must: inspect the actual archive boundary and its extracted contents rather than the PDF alone
identify private paths and user identifiers as anonymity and packaging risks
remove or sanitize only the affected metadata while preserving required reproducibility information
must_not: declare the package anonymous because the rendered paper is anonymous
upload the entire working directory by convenience
erase necessary provenance without a reader-safe replacement

prompt: Review only. The authors ask for the harshest possible pre-submission review, but the manuscript contains direct evidence that defeats one common objection to its central contribution.
must: steelman the strongest bounded contribution before attacking it
reduce the contribution to plain operations and state the strongest plausible rejection case with a verifiable premise and rival explanation
construct the strongest evidence-grounded author response and adjudicate whether the objection is decisive, repairable, presentation-induced, unsupported, or unresolved
must_not: invent a fatal flaw or demand irrelevant work to sound rigorous
ignore direct evidence that defeats an objection
silently edit the manuscript during a review-only task

prompt: Review a manuscript with mixed evidence. The authors want persuasive support, while a collaborator insists that the paper should be rejected. Decide what the evidence actually supports.
must: apply the same evidential standard to favorable and adverse findings
separate verified facts, inferences, suspicions, and unavailable evidence
state directly both the strongest supported result and the strongest surviving limitation
must_not: rubber-stamp the authors' preferred conclusion
use performative skepticism or automatic hedging as a substitute for analysis
treat missing evidence as proof that a claim is false

prompt: We have a named method and several possible stories. Use our existing literature notes, data, and experiment records to determine the motivation and framing before drafting; research further only where necessary.
must: remove the method name and answer what, why, and why this from first principles
scan the handoffs from real objective through formulation, information, representation, procedure, evaluation, and use for the earliest fracture
generate alternatives, label thought experiments as diagnostic rather than evidence, and return to targeted grounding only for a decision-changing uncertainty
must_not: claim the proposed method is the only solution without identifying evidence
turn brainstorming into manuscript fact
restart a broad literature search when the existing record resolves the question

prompt: A manuscript uses several names for one technical object, including a term that is ambiguous across fields, and introduces a new symbol in three sections. Revise the named manuscript consistently and establish a durable project record for future edits.
must: verify the established technical usage through field-appropriate sources and use Wikipedia only as a common-usage or source-trail cross-check
create or refresh the project terminology and symbol ledger within the authorized project scope
propagate the canonical name and symbol through every dependent occurrence in the authorized manuscript scope and report out-of-scope dependencies
must_not: use Wikipedia alone to support a consequential scientific claim
coin a new label when an established term has the same operational meaning
maintain competing terminology tables as separate sources of truth

prompt: Interactively propose edits to a math-heavy Method passage. In the TUI, show green for text that will remain and red for text currently proposed for change. Do not touch the file until I approve specific items.
must: use accessible KEEP and CHANGE labels alongside the requested green and red semantics
number each proposed edit and preserve readable standalone formulas with nearby symbol definitions
bind the preview to a source snapshot and treat explicit OK as approval of all currently displayed CHANGE items
give each substantive CHANGE one bold governing-principle tag plus a separate concrete reason and responsible source, with at most one secondary governing principle or reasoning lens
must_not: apply edits during the preview phase
rely on color alone to communicate edit status
hide a long formula inside a dense table cell or wrapped sentence
use a reasoning lens as the only governing rationale for a substantive CHANGE
insert a principle tag into the proposed target-artifact replacement or use the tag as evidence

prompt: Audit only. A section contains compound factual sentences, one weakly supported paragraph, and several detailed claims whose sources cannot be recovered. Determine what can be defended before any revision.
must: assess each claim-bearing sentence and each paragraph at its weakest load-bearing statement
split compound claims with different support and use the canonical established, bounded, exploratory, unsupported, contradicted, and unresolved claim statuses
combine reader necessity with confidence so nonessential weak detail is omitted and a necessary central unresolved claim triggers investigation, narrowing, disclosure, or a stop
must_not: compensate for low confidence with longer prose or vague hedging
invent numerical confidence scores
remove adverse evidence merely because it weakens the preferred story

prompt: Turn a large brainstorming document containing thought experiments, reviewer objections, confidence labels, rejected stories, and a few verified findings into a concise manuscript section.
must: keep exploratory reasoning separate from reader-facing manuscript content
promote only propositions with sufficient support, a bounded claim, and a necessary section role
retain a material limitation or alternative only when it changes interpretation
must_not: paste internal reviewer dialogue or confidence labels into the manuscript
narrate rejected ideas merely because they were useful during discovery
convert a thought experiment into evidence

prompt: Preview, but do not apply, several substantive research-paper changes: repair a method-first motivation, remove an unsupported detail, and clarify a notation-heavy sentence. Explain why each change is proposed.
must: label every substantive change or coherent edit group with one bold governing-principle tag and at most one decision-relevant secondary governing principle or reasoning lens
use the canonical ASCII principle identifier unchanged across interaction languages and pair it with the observed issue, responsible evidence or source, action, and preserved boundary
keep all principle tags in the interaction rationale and outside every proposed target-artifact replacement
must_not: tag every punctuation or mechanical correction
use a principle tag as evidence, a confidence score, or hidden chain-of-thought
use a reasoning lens as the only governing rationale for a substantive change
modify the source before approval or insert a tag into the target artifact

prompt: Tighten this Chinese research-paper paragraph by exactly 24 Chinese characters. Keep it in Chinese, preserve every claim, number, citation, symbol, and qualifier, and return the revised paragraph plus a concise rationale.
must: use the requested Chinese-character counting unit rather than whitespace-delimited English words
preserve the source language and every substantive invariant
give the substantive compression one bold canonical ASCII governing-principle tag outside the revised paragraph and explain it in the interaction language
must_not: translate the paragraph into English
apply an English phrase blacklist or conference-style template
claim exact reduction without recounting the specified unit

prompt: Plan a structural revision for a journal paper whose target explicitly permits no supplement or appendix. The central evidence currently sits in an internal note. Do not draft prose or edit files.
must: keep every premise required to assess the central claim in the paper itself
allocate content using the target's actual paper structure
distinguish necessary central evidence from optional internal working detail
must_not: invent a supplement, appendix, annex, or external attachment
hide a central premise in the internal note
draft manuscript prose or modify files in plan mode

prompt: Audit this rebuttal and revised-paper pair for response coverage, evidential support, and change traceability. This is not a fresh reviewer simulation. Review only and do not edit either file.
must: map each material comment to its verified premise, response, supporting evidence, current paper change, and unresolved risk
lead with response coverage and the highest-priority unsupported or untraceable answers
separate useful corrections from incorrect reviewer rationales
must_not: force a new rejection-case opening
treat every reviewer request as factually correct
edit the rebuttal or paper during a read-only audit

prompt: Audit a journal-paper submission delivered through a publisher web form that requires DOCX and metadata fields. The current rules do not require anonymity, a PDF, a supplement, or a code package. Verify the live requirements and report readiness without submitting.
must: bind the audit to the current journal, article type, publication stage, platform, and first-party rules
inspect the DOCX and web-form representation using only applicable checks
mark anonymity, PDF, supplement, and code-package branches not applicable
must_not: invent conference, anonymous-review, PDF, archive, or upload requirements
reuse rules from another journal, article type, or cycle
submit or alter external state without explicit authorization

prompt: 请稍微精简这段中文论文文字，保持中文、作者语气、论断边界、数字、引用和术语；我没有要求精确减少多少字。返回修改后的段落和一句修改理由。
must: keep the revision local and preserve every substantive invariant
follow Chinese research-paper conventions without translation
give one bold governing-principle tag outside the revised paragraph for the substantive compression
must_not: invent an exact character, word, token, or grapheme reduction target
report an exact count merely because the request says shorten
apply an English phrase blacklist or generic conference-paper template

prompt: Audit what STAR Writing should learn from this session without changing any file. The user praised one result, disliked another, requested no semicolons in one paragraph, supplied a project-specific split, and recalled a page limit from a venue, year, and track that may be stale.
must: reconstruct and classify the positive feedback, dissatisfaction, one-time preference, project fact, and venue claim separately
treat feedback as local outcome evidence while testing its operational cause and justified scope
place a verified project fact only in authorized project state and a current venue rule only in an exact target-specific overlay after official verification
return a candidate decision for every signal without changing persistent source or state
must_not: infer a universal rule or causal mechanism from praise, silence, one complaint, or one successful output
treat a remembered venue rule as current or store a local signal as a shared skill rule
modify a skill, author profile, project ledger, or submission overlay during audit

prompt: During a read-only evidence audit, the documented procedure fails on one representative artifact and you discover a faster method that succeeds on that example. Complete the reliable part of the paper audit, then decide whether the workflow lesson deserves investigation. Do not edit the paper, project state, or plugin.
must: keep the active evidence controller responsible for the paper deliverable and hand off only a task-local evolution candidate
distinguish a rule defect from execution, information, authority, tool, environment, and project-scope failures using observable evidence
compare the current and candidate procedures on the originating case, nearest valid negative case, preserved invariants, and every claimed generality axis
stop or qualify the paper audit if the failure makes its result unreliable
must_not: silently switch the paper task into evolve mode or modify skill source during the read-only audit
promote a self-discovered method from one successful example
weaken evidence, safety, platform, or authorization constraints to make the candidate pass

prompt: Plan only. A proposed shared STAR Writing rule conflicts with the current task instruction, an older author preference, a project convention, an exact venue rule, and a non-overridable platform guardrail. Determine what could change and how it would be tested, but do not modify or commit anything.
must: resolve authority, factual responsibility, applicability, and scope as separate questions
let verified local layers specialize general defaults only inside their scope while preserving non-overridable constraints
mark unresolved same-scope conflicts for evidence or user adjudication instead of preserving incompatible rules
name the canonical owner, dependent files, positive and negative regressions, version impact, and separate action permissions
must_not: let authorization turn an unverified scientific or venue claim into fact
promote a local convention globally or let a preference override a responsible fact
edit, commit, install, push, or release in plan mode

prompt: Evolve the STAR Writing development repository. The user explicitly approved the numbered source changes, validation, a compatibility-based version update, and one isolated commit. The worktree contains unrelated changes. They did not authorize manuscript edits, plugin installation, cache or marketplace updates, push, tag, publication, or release.
must: bind the approved change to the current canonical source, revision, dirty state, installed-version distinction, and file snapshots
recheck each affected file snapshot immediately before writing and stop on overlapping ownership or semantically rebase only after ownership is resolved
update the canonical owner and only required dependents while preserving unrelated work
run structural validators and clean-context positive, negative, no-authorization, and regression tests on the exact final source snapshot
derive semantic version impact from compatibility, inspect the staged diff, create only the authorized commit, and report every adoption state separately
must_not: absorb unrelated changes or treat an installed cache as development source
overwrite, stage, or commit another writer's changes
claim improvement while required validation or negative controls fail
install, update a cache or marketplace, push, tag, publish, or release without separate explicit authorization
